basis: Legionella infection includes pneumonic Legionnaires' disease and nonpneumonic Pontiac fever; pulmonary damage is not established as typical across the umbrella.

decisions.pulmonary: none: pneumonia defines one subtype; nonpneumonic Pontiac fever prevents assuming pulmonary damage is typical across legionellosis.

basis: Autoimmune thrombophilia with vascular thrombosis; cerebral infarction causes direct brain injury in approximately 50-60% of reported symptomatic neonatal cases.

decisions.neurologic: involved: cerebral infarction occurs in approximately 50-60% of reported neonatal APS cases, exceeding the threshold.

basis: Enteric Yersinia infections account for most clinical yersiniosis; direct intestinal inflammation exceeds 30% across the group. Plague-specific damage is not generalized.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: enterocolitica and pseudotuberculosis enteric infections dominate clinical yersiniosis, making intestinal inflammation common overall (>30%).

basis: Larval migration causes destructive CNS inflammation in most recognized symptomatic cases (>30%); ocular and visceral injury are less consistently documented.

decisions.neurologic: involved: neural larva migrans causes lasting brain injury in most recognized symptomatic cases, exceeding 30%; subclinical infections create uncertainty.

basis: GPI-anchor disorder with ID; shortened phalanges 2/2 and severe enteric malformations 1/2. Strabismus 2/3, hearing loss and ASD 1/2 omitted by cap, prioritizing severe bowel damage.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: anal stenosis and aganglionic megacolon each occur in 1/2 assessed patients and represent substantial structural or functional bowel damage.
decisions.ocular: none at cap: strabismus 2/3 qualifies, but skeletal abnormalities 2/2 and severe enteric malformations 1/2 take priority.

basis: Presynaptic NMJ and CNS disorder; fixed knee flexion contracture in 1/1 reported patient supports structural musculoskeletal involvement, with substantial small-sample uncertainty.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: fixed knee flexion contracture is structural joint dysfunction, reported in 1/1 patient; weakness alone would not qualify.

basis: Defined by nail aplasia and persistent skin abnormalities. Caries in 80-99% is a separate dental disease; intrinsic developmental tooth damage is not established.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: frequent caries (80-99%) is separately diagnosed dental disease; the evidence does not establish intrinsic tooth malformation or direct syndromic dental injury.

basis: Mitochondrial lactic acidosis with defining brain defects and brachydactyly; PDA 1/1. Hepatic enzyme/complex abnormalities alone do not establish functional liver damage.

decisions.hepatic: none: transaminase elevation and reduced respiratory-chain activity in liver do not establish sustained hepatic dysfunction or structural damage.
decisions.cardiovascular: involved: patent ductus arteriosus is a structural cardiovascular abnormality reported in 1/1 patient; frequency evidence is limited to this case.
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: brachydactyly is explicitly part of the defining syndrome and occurs in 1/1 patient; it represents structural bone abnormality.

basis: Inherited infection-triggered encephalopathy in 8/8; cataracts in 2/2 assessed support ocular involvement. Infection susceptibility alone does not establish an immune disorder.

decisions.infectious_immune: none: an infection-triggered inherited encephalopathy is not itself an infection or established immunodeficiency; the record does not establish an immune-mediated mechanism.

basis: Vascular neoplasm arising in and occupying the laryngeal/tracheal airway. Facial hemangioma occurs in only 5-29%; feeding difficulty does not establish digestive injury.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: angioma is a neoplasm of blood vessels, giving vascular origin in addition to its laryngeal/tracheal location.
